voronoi_strands.name: Voronoi Strands
voronoi_strands.description: An open three-dimensional Voronoi edge skeleton drawn in thin charcoal tubes, with shared junctions and cords anchored directly to surrounding floors, walls and ceilings. Seeded sites define the cell geometry. No opaque cell faces or line collision. An enlarged eight-legged spider lays the lines progressively, tracing the mathematical graph as an artwork rather than simulating natural web growth. All strands belong to one connected graph with shared 3D junctions and explicit attachments to room surfaces. The completed net relaxes under gravity with tension-only cables, fixed room anchors and unbreakable shared knots.
voronoi_strands.qfep_connection: A partition remains legible as lines while its faces no longer bar passage. The attachment cords depend on the host architecture. Releasing the net distinguishes its distance construction from its shape under load: shared knots transmit a pull while fixed room anchors carry it.

parameters.anchors: 0–64 tethers to existing floors, walls and ceilings
parameters.surface_reach: Maximum surface search distance in metres, 5 to 100
parameters.weave: Build progressively with a spider; false immediately releases the complete net
parameters.weave_speed: Spider travel speed in metres per second, 0.1 to 20
parameters.tension: Release the completed net under gravity; false preserves the Voronoi construction
parameters.compliance: Cable stretch per newton, 0.000001 to 0.001 m/N
parameters.knot_mass: Mass per free shared knot, 0.001 to 0.1 kg

interactions: Walk around and through the open structure
Inspect the polygon edges from different viewpoints
Watch the spider lay strands and retrace completed branches
Highlight shared junctions with Space in the standalone preview
F finishes and releases the net; G tugs a knot; P pauses forces
